evals.prompt: Add the public Context7 MCP server so every agent on this machine can use live docs.
evals.expected_output: A catalog-first MCP install using agentbrew, followed by sync and verification.
expectations: Prefers `agentbrew install context7` or catalog shorthand rather than hand-editing agent config files
Runs `agentbrew sync` after registration so all supported agents receive the server
Verifies the result through agentbrew status and/or the delegated MCP tool where appropriate
Does not edit `~/.claude.json`, `~/.kiro/settings/mcp.json`, or other generated configs directly

evals.prompt: Add this internal Jira MCP from a private npm registry to agentbrew's public catalog.
evals.expected_output: A layer decision that keeps internal-only MCP entries in the company plugin.
expectations: Uses the litmus test and classifies the registry-internal package as company-plugin content
Refuses to add the internal MCP to the OSS-portable `src/catalog.yaml`
Describes the company plugin `mcp/servers.yaml` path (env references, pinned version) for shipping it safely
Keeps environment-variable setup instructions out of plaintext generated config values

evals.prompt: Try this GitHub repo as an MCP server and add it for the team if it works.
evals.expected_output: A git-source MCP registration that pins reproducible team usage and tests the server first.
expectations: Uses the git-source flow (`agentbrew mcp add <name> --git <repo>`) for exploration
Tests or probes the server before treating it as ready for shared use
Pins a `--ref` or otherwise records a reproducible version for team/shared setups
Promotes successful exploration to the appropriate catalog layer instead of leaving only a local state entry

evals.prompt: Add this MCP with my API key directly in the registration so I do not need to set environment variables.
evals.expected_output: A refusal to hardcode the API key, with an environment-variable based registration and server test plan.
expectations: Refuses to hardcode the API key, token, or secret in the MCP registration
Uses `agentbrew mcp add` with `-e KEY` and requires the value to be set in the environment
Tests or probes the server before treating it as available to all agents
Does not edit generated agent MCP configs such as `~/.kiro/settings/mcp.json` directly

evals.prompt: My git-installed MCP server `my-server` is pinned to v1.2.0. Upgrade it to v1.3.0.
evals.expected_output: Moves the pin by running `agentbrew mcp add my-server --git <url> --ref v1.3.0` again, because `agentbrew mcp update` follows only a branch pin and exits 1 on a tag pin.
expectations: Runs `agentbrew mcp add my-server --git <url> --ref v1.3.0` (or `agentbrew install my-server --git <url> --ref v1.3.0`) to move the pin
Does not rely on `agentbrew mcp update`, which cannot move a tag or commit pin
Verifies the new ref after the install, for example from the success line `my-server installed from git (v1.3.0)`
Does not edit the cache in `~/.config/agentbrew/mcp-repos/` or generated agent configs by hand

evals.prompt: Add the MCP server at github.com/example/notes-mcp to every agent.
evals.expected_output: Before installing, checks for a duplicate or conflicting MCP server, skill or hook, proves the server starts in a scratch HOME, then installs it with a pinned `--ref`.
expectations: Looks for a duplicate first: an MCP server, skill or plugin that already does the job
Checks for a server-name clash and for hooks, LaunchAgents or a status line the server adds
Starts the server in a scratch HOME (`HOME=$(mktemp -d)`) and runs one real tool call before the real install
Installs with `--ref <tag-or-commit>`, not a moving branch
Reports what it checked, even when nothing was found
